# Agentsol

> Agentsol is a free, MIT-licensed MCP server and CLI (npm package `agentsol`, early alpha) that reviews AI coding agents' work: the instruction files they follow (AGENTS.md, AGENTS.override.md, CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and SKILL.md), what they did in recent Claude Code and Codex sessions, and how the AI apps on the machine are set up. It runs locally, uses the person's own assistant (no API key, no hosted service), cites exact lines for every finding, and only proposes diffs. A person approves and applies changes in their own terminal; there is no MCP tool for approval.

## Install (any MCP client)

- Command: `npx`, args: `-y -p agentsol@alpha agentsol-mcp` (workspace defaults to `<home>/.agentsol`; override with `AGENTSOL_WORKSPACE`)
- Claude Code: `claude mcp add agentsol -s user -- npx -y -p agentsol@alpha agentsol-mcp`
- Codex: `codex mcp add agentsol -- npx -y -p agentsol@alpha agentsol-mcp`
- Gemini CLI: `gemini mcp add -s user agentsol npx -y -p agentsol@alpha agentsol-mcp`
- A person sets up each project first, inside it: `npx -y agentsol@alpha start` (registers and scans it, and connects installed apps after asking). `check` is the scan alone.
- Web chats without MCP: `npx -y agentsol@alpha prompt` prints one masked prompt to paste.
- Sessions: `npx -y agentsol@alpha sessions` and `npx -y agentsol@alpha session <id> --timeline`
- Setup audit: `npx -y agentsol@alpha doctor`
- Requires Node.js 24 or newer.

## MCP prompts and resources

- Prompts: `audit` (full audit), `fix` (turn findings into proposals), `explain` (which instruction files apply to a path), `review` (grade recent sessions on the rubric), `setup` (explain the setup audit), `learn` (turn repeated agent mistakes into rules for AGENTS.md)
- Resource: `agentsol://guide` (workflow and check catalogue)

## MCP tools

projects_list, workspace_status, sources_freshness, sources_scan, sources_list, source_read, scope_resolve, checks_run, findings_list, findings_submit, change_propose, changes_list, change_status, sessions_list, session_review, session_grade, setup_audit, inspect, lessons_list, project_briefing, command_check

## Workflow for agents

0. Starting work in a project? Call project_briefing with path set to your working folder (it can be left out when the server started in the project, as in Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI; in Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code and Claude Desktop pass it) and follow it: rules from mistakes agents repeated there, out-of-date instruction lines with what to do instead, and commands to ask the user about. Before a build, test, install or deploy command, call command_check: verdict change gives the command that works here, ask means ask the user first. Read-only.
1. projects_list, then sources_scan and findings_list. Structural findings are facts.
2. source_read for numbered, masked lines and the current versionId.
3. findings_submit for POSSIBLE issues, always with exact quoted evidence.
4. change_propose for fixes. Never edit instruction files directly.
5. Tell the user to run `npx agentsol review <proposalId>` in their own terminal.
6. sessions_list and session_review report what agents did (checks A01-A14, facts). session_grade stores your rubric grade (safety, instructions, verification, efficiency, scope; 1-5 each), citing real step numbers. It is labelled assistant judgment.
7. setup_audit reports AI app settings (checks C01-C10): plaintext secrets, unpinned or missing MCP servers, permissions that skip confirmation, hooks. Explain; never change settings.
8. Session and setup tools return derived facts only, never transcript text, tool output or secret values. Over MCP, only sessions inside registered projects are visible.
9. inspect checks a skill or MCP server before it is installed: pass its files as text (SKILL.md and scripts, or a tools/list JSON). Verdict danger, caution or clean, with findings by file and line. Needs no registered project. Also on the web and as `npx agentsol@alpha inspect <folder>`.
10. lessons_list finds mistakes agents repeated in a project across Claude Code and Codex sessions (a command that fails and the one that works, files they keep breaking, things the user told them more than once), with the time and tokens lost and one rule per lesson. It also lists conflicts: lines in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md that tell agents to run the failing command, each with the corrected line (including lines that contradict something the user said more than once), and says why a written rule did not help (for example, Codex does not read CLAUDE.md). Pass suggestedChange and each otherChanges entry to change_propose, one call each; never edit instruction files directly. Also `npx agentsol@alpha learn [--propose]`. It reads the last 180 days unless since says otherwise. Sessions started in a parent or sibling folder count with only their steps in the project, and a lesson whose command later ran fine as written is dropped.
